# GitLite Docs

> API documentation for GitLite, a Gitea fork

- Documentation: https://gitlite-docs.thally.app
- GitHub: https://github.com/vaibhav700c/gitlite-docs
- Full docs for LLMs: https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/llms-full.txt
- Agent discovery (ai.txt): https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/ai.txt
- Structured docs index (JSON): https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/api/docs-index
- OpenAPI spec: https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/openapi.yaml

## For AI agents

Every page supports content negotiation on its human URL:
- JSON API: append `?format=json` or send `Accept: application/json`
- JSON-LD: append `?format=ldjson` or send `Accept: application/ld+json`
- Markdown: append `?format=md` or send `Accept: text/markdown`
- Per-page API: https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/api/docs/{page-id}
- Search API: https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/api/search?q={query}
- Capability manifest (skill): https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/skill.md
- Agent guidance (editing these docs): https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/AGENTS.md
- MCP server (attach docs as native tools): https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/api/mcp
- Agent readiness: https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/api/agent-readiness

### Recommended workflow

1. Use this index, the search API, or `search_docs` before choosing a page.
2. Read the smallest set of relevant pages and follow their prerequisite links.
3. Treat the published docs as the source of truth. Label inferences and say when evidence is missing.
4. Cite the canonical human page URLs, not only API endpoints.
5. Use `/AGENTS.md` before editing a repository. The public MCP server is read-only.

## Documentation

### Getting Started

- [Introduction](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/): GitLite is a self-hosted Git service with a REST API. Start here to find the right guide.
- [Quickstart](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/quickstart): Make your first authenticated GitLite API call and create a repository in about a minute.
- [Authentication](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/authentication): Authenticate with the GitLite API. Create access tokens, send them in the Authorization header, and choose token scopes.
- [Pagination](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/pagination): Read long lists from the GitLite API with page and limit, and use the Link, X-Total-Count, X-Page, X-PerPage, and X-HasMore headers.

### Guides

- [Guide: Handling errors](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/guides/errors): Interpret GitLite API status codes, error bodies, and authentication failures, and decide when to retry.
- [Guide: Rate limits and response size](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/guides/rate-limits): Understand how GitLite caps page size and response size, and how to write clients that stay within those caps.
- [Guide: Webhooks](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/guides/webhooks): Receive HTTP callbacks from GitLite when events such as pushes and issue changes happen in a repository.
- [Guide: Deployment](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/guides/deployment): Build the GitLite binary from source and run it with SQLite for development or a small team.

### Reference

- [API reference: Repositories](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/api/repositories): List, create, read, and update repositories with the GitLite REST API.
- [API reference: Issues](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/api/issues): List, create, read, and update repository issues with the GitLite REST API.
- [API reference: Organizations](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/api/organizations): List, create, and read organizations and their repositories with the GitLite REST API.
- [Configuration reference: [api]](https://gitlite-docs.thally.app/reference/configuration-api): Every key in the [api] section of GitLite's app.ini, with its default and effect on API clients.
